newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN RUPEE EDGES UP VS FWD DLR, QUIET IN SPOT.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN RUPEE EDGES UP VS FWD DLR, QUIET IN SPOT.

text.p: The Indian rupee edged up slightly against the forward dollar in late morning trade Thursday but was stuck in a groove in the spot market, dealers said.
January-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 0.82/0.85 rupees against Wednesday's close of 0.86/89.
"There has been some selling at higher levels," said a foreign bank dealer. "Premiums have come down and the trend looks soft."
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had not yet made an appearance on Thursday.
RBI bought both spot and forward dollars from Monday and while forward premiums have gone up from last week's levels, the rupee has remained buoyant in the spot market.
In latest deals, the spot rupee was quoted 35.72/73 per dollar.
"There are bids at 35.72 and offers at 35.73," said a dealer. "The market has been pretty much at the same level through the morning."
"The market will remain quiet unless the RBI comes in."
